newsitem.title: INDIA: India 97/98 Q1 oil imports dip.
newsitem.headline: India 97/98 Q1 oil imports dip.

text.p: India's oil imports during the first quarter of 1997/98 (April-March) dipped to $2.01 billion from $2.20 billion in the same period last year, an official said on Monday.

"The total import volume during the first quarter of the current financial year was lower at 13.10 million tonnes compared to 13.57 million tonnes last year," Nirmal Singh, a senior Petroleum Ministry official told Reuters.

Of the total imports, crude oil volumes were higher at 8.18 million tonnes in the current year against 7.95 million last year. However, outflow of foreign exchange on crude imports was stagnant at $1.08 billion in both periods, Singh said.

He said import of petroleum products declined to 4.91 million tonnes from 5.62 million a year earlier. "Forex outflow for product imports fell to $925.84 million in April-June 1997 from $1,114.93 million in April-June 1996," he added.
India imports diesel, kerosene, motor spirit, liquefied petroleum gas, fuel oil and aviation turbine fuel.

According to preliminary Petroleum Ministry estimates, India will import 33.66 million tonnes of crude oil and 24.79 million tonnes of petroleum products during 1997-98 (April-March). The import bill for the year has been pegged at $10.14 billion.
During 1996-97 (April-March), the country spent $9.33 billion on import of 33.90 million tonnes of crude oil and 19.49 million tonnes of petroleum products.
-- Amitav Ranjan, New Delhi Newsroom (91) 11-301-2024; Fax (91) 11-301-4043
